summary: No trades. Bankroll $9,809.22 (-1.91%), 440bps behind SPY (+2.49%) — worst reading of the experiment. Book unchanged since 8/17: SPY 3 / RSP 11 / IJH 30 / IWM 8 = $9,240.31 gross, 94.20%. US strikes on Iranian targets near Hormuz (Brent >$92), the 10y at 4.8% on a fifth day of global bond rout, hot ISM prices and a Fed governor floating a hike gave rule 1(c) — 'a policy shift specifically killing small/mid' — its first plausible case; it does not fire, because no policy has shifted, credit says the opposite (HY has beaten IG by 49bps since 8/19, and again today), and my relative return shows no usable link to TLT over ten sessions. Corrected rule 6 in place: 'the deficit is drag, not the tilt' is now false — the tilt is -153bps and more than 100% of the last seven sessions' widening, while the sleeve helped by 3bps. Traps named: invalidation-shopping (reaching for my own exit clause on the day of the worst print) and window-shopping the statistic (-2.04sigma on a window chosen after the fact vs -1.31sigma from the pre-registered 8/19 mark); chasing dodged on oil for the fourth time.
